title: Polynomial-time indexed bit read
statement: Let $f$ map bit strings to bit strings and let $i$ assign a natural-number index to each bit string. If $f$ is polynomial-time computable and the unary word of length $i(x)$ is polynomial-time computable from $x$, then the function returning the bit of $f(x)$ at index $i(x)$, with false as the default when that index is out of range, is polynomial-time computable.
replaced: If a word producer and a unary index producer are polynomial-time computable, then the single-bit read of the produced word at the produced index, with false as out-of-range default, is polynomial-time computable.
